cross_references.title: California Penal Code § 502
cross_references.relationship: State parallel. CFAA provides federal jurisdiction; § 502 provides California state jurisdiction and a private right of action. Both can be pursued simultaneously for the same unauthorized access.

cross_references.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1343 — Wire Fraud
cross_references.relationship: SIM swap fraud typically involves wire communications (phone networks). The CFAA violations establish the unauthorized access; § 1343 wire fraud covers the fraudulent scheme that the access was in furtherance of. Wire fraud is a RICO predicate; CFAA alone is not.

cross_references.title: 47 U.S.C. § 222 — CPNI
cross_references.relationship: The CFAA violation (unauthorized computer access) is enabled by the § 222 violation (carrier's failure to authenticate before SIM change). Sequential: § 222 breach → carrier grants unauthorized access → CFAA unauthorized access occurs.

cross_references.title: Van Buren v. United States (2021) 593 U.S. 374
cross_references.relationship: SCOTUS decision narrowing CFAA 'exceeds authorized access' to mean accessing areas one lacks permission to access (not violating use restrictions). Does not affect pure unauthorized-access cases like SIM swap attacks.
